just re-reading this thread, and not sure if serious. If so, which plants? looks like you talking about tomatoes, but i saw where you said take the first few flowers off the peppers.

I was talking about flicking your tomato flowers. Also shaking them works too. Low harvest can be a number of issues like no pollination (that's what the flicking helps because tomato flowers pollinate themselves but if there's not a lot of wind they won't pollinate) also low nutrients or low sunlight can play a role.

For peppers yes I recommend removing the first few blossoms/fruit. This helps the plant focus on building leaves and stems. The theory behind this is that it helps the plant build a better base to allow bigger more plentiful fruit a little later on. But with that said different strokes for different folks so do what works for you!
